# fin.dated_charges

An immutable date-banded fee table: a standing charge that changes on given dates.

## Overview

`fin.dated_charges` is owned by the [`fin`](../stdlib/fin.md) module (see [Rate and charge
tables](../stdlib/fin.md#rate-and-charge-tables) for what the four tables share). It is built from a one-line text
form or from band records:

| text form | band record |
| --- | --- |
| `"2024-01-01:25.00, 2025-01-01:30.00"` | `{from: date, amount}` |

A dated charge has no `apply` member (`dc.apply(…)` is `invalid_method`).

<a id="array"></a>
### `array([default]) -> array`

Answer a new one-element `array` holding the receiver.

Total, so the default is never used.

```go
import("fin").dated_charges().array()   // => [fin.dated_charges("0001-01-01:0")]
```

<a id="at"></a>
### `at(on[, fallback]) -> decimal`

Answer the amount in force on the date `on`; `fallback` answers **only** a date before the first band.

```go
fin := import("fin")
dc := fin.dated_charges("2026-01-01:25, 2026-07-01:30")
dc.at(d"2025-12-31")                            // Error: invalid_value: (at) no band covers the argument
dc.at(d"2025-12-31", 20)                        // => 20d — the fallback, before the first band only
dc.at(d"2026-08-01", 20)                        // => 30d
```

<a id="bands"></a>
### `bands() -> array`

Answer the bands as records in constructor shape, so the table rebuilds from them: `fin.dated_charges(t.bands()) == t`.

<a id="copy"></a>
### `copy() -> fin.dated_charges`

Answer the table itself — it is immutable.
